correctness.rationale: For k>=3 and ai>0 with L=sum_i ai, independently obtained convolution density: f(t)=2/L + k(k-3)t/L^2 - 2(k-2)/L^2 sum(t-ai)_+ + 2/L^2 sum_{i<j}(t-ai-aj)_+. At origin f(0+)=2/L and slope f′(0+)=k(k-3)/L^2, strictly determining L and k for integers k>=3. Distributional curvature μ=L^2 f″ = -2(k-2)sum δ_ai +2sum δ_ai+aj. A peeling algorithm subtracts the already recovered arm singleton/pair contributions; its smallest nonzero remaining support is always a negative atom at the least unrecovered positive length, as every remaining cross pair is strictly larger. Its integer mass fixes multiplicity, including coincident original cancellations. Termination after k copies proves uniqueness for arbitrary real positive lengths, not just rational tests. Independent Fraction checks compared direct same-arm/cross-arm densities to spline for 597 cases and reconstructed examples incl. (1,2,3) cancellation. The k<=2 interval exception has identical distance law for arbitrary splitting.

value.rationale: Unlabeled pairwise metric distance is a fundamental graph sampling invariant. Recovering unknown arm count and ALL positive lengths from a single exact population distribution—even under cancellation of curvature breakpoints—solves a natural inverse problem with a constructive robust-in-algebra, though not statistically stable, procedure.

limitations: No arbitrary graph identifiability, no noisy samples or stability estimate, k<=2 is an interval and arms not identifiable.
